query: Queueing and scheduling in shared automated laboratories and in flexible job shops with transport robots: how waiting time and throughput depend on the number of transport robots or AGVs, on a single shared transfer point, and on instruments that block for hours; effect of adding external or multi-user load to an automated lab or cloud lab (utilization against waiting, scheduling policies, priority between internal and external work); evidence on whether transport or instrument time is the bottleneck in laboratory automation, and published rules for sizing the number of mobile robots.
